tracks.title: Foundations
tracks.blurb: The language, the math and the tools.

tracks.title: Core machine learning
tracks.blurb: How models learn, from linear regression to Transformers.

tracks.title: Specializations
tracks.blurb: Vision, language, LLMs, generation, decision-making and robots.

tracks.title: Production
tracks.blurb: Shipping, securing and scaling AI systems.

courses.title: Python for AI
courses.tagline: The language every AI system is written in.
courses.description: A practical Python course aimed at AI work: values and functions, containers, classes, generators, files, environments and concurrency. Start here if you are new to programming or want to fill gaps.
outcomes: Write clean, idiomatic Python with functions, classes and comprehensions
Pick the right data structure and reason about its cost
Use generators, decorators and type hints the way ML libraries do
Manage environments and dependencies, and handle errors and files
Run thousands of API calls concurrently with asyncio

lessons.title: Python Essentials: Values, Control Flow & Functions
lessons.lead: Everything in AI code starts here: how Python represents data, makes decisions, repeats work and packages logic into functions.

lessons.title: Lists, Dicts, Sets & Comprehensions
lessons.lead: The four built-in containers carry almost all data in ordinary Python. Choosing the right one is often the difference between a script that takes seconds and one that takes hours.

lessons.title: Classes, Dataclasses & the Python Data Model
lessons.lead: PyTorch modules, datasets, tokenizers and API clients are all classes. Understanding how Python objects work makes every framework feel familiar.

toc.text: Class attributes, class methods and static methods

lessons.title: Iterators, Generators, Decorators & Type Hints
lessons.lead: The tools behind data loaders, streaming LLM responses, retry logic and readable code: lazy iteration, functions that wrap functions, and types that document intent.

lessons.title: Files, Errors, Environments & Packaging
lessons.lead: Real projects read and write files, fail in interesting ways, and must run on someone else's machine. This lesson covers the plumbing that makes code dependable.

lessons.title: Concurrency: Threads, Processes & asyncio
lessons.lead: Calling an LLM API 10,000 times one by one takes hours; doing it concurrently takes minutes. Learn which kind of concurrency fits which kind of work.

courses.title: Mathematics for AI
courses.tagline: Linear algebra, calculus, probability and optimization, derived step by step.
courses.description: The math that every later course leans on, taught with intuition first and derivations second. You will see where each idea shows up in real models.
outcomes: Work fluently with vectors, matrices, eigenvalues and the SVD
Derive gradients with the chain rule and matrix calculus
Reason with probability, Bayes, and maximum likelihood
Explain cross-entropy, KL divergence and why losses are likelihoods
Understand gradient descent, Adam, numerical precision and Monte Carlo

lessons.title: Vectors, Norms & Dot Products
lessons.lead: Every input an AI model sees (an image, a sentence, a user profile) becomes a vector. Geometry on vectors is the native language of ML.

lessons.title: Matrices & Linear Maps
lessons.lead: A matrix is a function: it takes a vector in and gives a vector out, linearly. A neural network layer is exactly this, plus a bias and a nonlinearity.

lessons.title: Eigenvalues, Eigenvectors & SVD
lessons.lead: Decompositions reveal what a matrix really does: stretch along special directions. They power PCA, LoRA, recommender systems and the analysis of training dynamics.

lessons.title: Calculus: Derivatives, Gradients & the Chain Rule
lessons.lead: Learning is nudging parameters in the direction that reduces the loss. Derivatives tell us that direction.

toc.text: Why the gradient is the direction of steepest ascent

lessons.title: Matrix Calculus for ML
lessons.lead: You need a handful of vector/matrix derivative identities to derive every gradient in this guide. Learn them once.

lessons.title: Probability: Random Variables, PDFs & Expectation
lessons.lead: Data is noisy and the future is uncertain. Probability gives us a calculus for uncertainty, and most ML models are, at heart, probability distributions.

lessons.title: Variance, Covariance & Joint Distributions
lessons.lead: Spread, co-movement, and how variables depend on each other.

lessons.title: Bayes' Theorem
lessons.lead: How to update beliefs with evidence. It underlies Naive Bayes, MAP estimation, Bayesian deep learning, and how to read any classifier's output correctly.

lessons.title: The Distributions You Need
lessons.lead: A short list of distributions covers almost all of ML. Each one corresponds to a loss function or a modelling choice.

lessons.title: Statistics: MLE, MAP & Where Loss Functions Come From
lessons.lead: This lesson connects statistics to deep learning. Common loss functions are not arbitrary: they are negative log-likelihoods.

lessons.title: Information Theory: Entropy, Cross-Entropy & KL
lessons.lead: The vocabulary of modern loss functions. Every LLM is trained to minimize a cross-entropy, and KL divergence appears in VAEs, RLHF, distillation and t-SNE.

lessons.title: Optimization: Gradient Descent to Adam
lessons.lead: Training a model means solving \(\min_\theta\mathcal L(\theta)\). Here is the toolkit and why each piece exists.

lessons.title: Numerical Computing: Floating Point & Stability
lessons.lead: Every model runs on finite-precision numbers. Knowing how floats break explains NaN losses, why bf16 took over training, and why every library implements softmax the "weird" way.

toc.text: Stable formulas to know by heart

lessons.title: Sampling, Monte Carlo & MCMC
lessons.lead: When an expectation or an integral can't be computed exactly, we estimate it with random samples. This idea is behind SGD, dropout, VAEs, diffusion sampling, RL and Bayesian inference.

courses.title: Programming & Data
courses.tagline: NumPy, pandas, PyTorch, SQL and the engineering habits that make ML code reliable.
courses.description: The day-to-day tools of an AI engineer: vectorized numerics, data exploration, leak-free preprocessing, PyTorch, algorithms for interviews, SQL and data pipelines, and testing ML code.
outcomes: Vectorize computations with NumPy broadcasting and einsum
Explore data with pandas and build leak-free preprocessing pipelines
Use PyTorch tensors, autograd, modules and data loaders
Solve common coding-interview problems
Query data with SQL and structure a testable ML project

lessons.title: Python & NumPy for ML
lessons.lead: Vectorization turns math on paper into fast code. A Python loop over a million elements is slow; one NumPy operation over the array is around 100× faster.

toc.text: Python essentials to be fluent in

lessons.title: pandas & Exploratory Data Analysis
lessons.lead: Before modelling, understand the data. Most real-world ML wins come from data understanding, not model choice.

lessons.title: Preprocessing, Feature Engineering & Leakage
lessons.lead: Models see only what you give them, in the scale you give it. Good features beat clever models; a leaky pipeline produces great validation scores and a useless model.

lessons.title: PyTorch Fundamentals
lessons.lead: PyTorch is NumPy on GPUs plus automatic differentiation. Once you understand tensors, autograd and nn.Module, every deep learning model is the same pattern.

lessons.title: Data Structures & Algorithms for AI Engineers
lessons.lead: Top-tier interviews still include coding rounds, and production ML code lives or dies on complexity. You need fluency with a core toolkit, not a competitive-programming career.

toc.text: The complexity table to know cold
Patterns that solve most interview problems
ML-flavoured problems you should be able to write from scratch

lessons.title: SQL & Data Engineering
lessons.lead: Most of an AI engineer's data starts in a database or a data lake. Fluent SQL and a mental model of data pipelines make you independent and fast.

toc.text: SQL you must be able to write

lessons.title: Software Engineering for ML
lessons.lead: What separates an AI engineer from someone who trains models in notebooks: code that is tested, reproducible, reviewable and fast.

courses.title: Classical Machine Learning
courses.tagline: From linear models to gradient boosting, plus forecasting, recommenders and experiments.
courses.description: The algorithms that still win on tabular data and the ideas every deep learning model builds on: generalization, regularization, evaluation, and how to run experiments that tell the truth.
outcomes: Derive and implement linear and logistic regression
Train and tune trees, random forests and gradient boosting
Cluster and reduce dimensionality with k-means, GMMs and PCA
Choose the right metric and validate without leakage
Forecast time series, build recommenders and run A/B tests

lessons.title: The Learning Framework: Generalization & Bias–Variance
lessons.lead: ML is not about fitting the training data. It is about performing well on data you haven't seen.

lessons.title: Linear Regression, Ridge & Lasso
lessons.lead: The simplest model, and the one where you can derive everything by hand.

lessons.title: Logistic Regression & Softmax
lessons.lead: Classification with probabilities. The softmax + cross-entropy combination here is the exact output layer of every classifier and every LLM.

lessons.title: k-Nearest Neighbours & Naive Bayes
lessons.lead: Two simple, strong baselines: one with no training at all, one built straight from Bayes' theorem.

lessons.title: Support Vector Machines & Kernels
lessons.lead: Find the separating hyperplane with the widest margin, then use the kernel trick to make it nonlinear without ever computing the features.

toc.text: Dual form and the kernel trick

lessons.title: Decision Trees, Random Forests & Gradient Boosting
lessons.lead: For tabular data, gradient-boosted trees (XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) are still usually the strongest models. Here is the math that makes them work.

lessons.title: Unsupervised Learning: k-Means, GMMs, EM & PCA
lessons.lead: Finding structure without labels: groups, densities and low-dimensional representations.

lessons.title: Evaluation Metrics
lessons.lead: The metric defines what "good" means. Choose it before you train.

lessons.title: Time Series & Forecasting
lessons.lead: Demand, traffic, energy, prices, sensor data: forecasting is one of the most common ML jobs in industry, and it breaks the i.i.d. assumption that most of Part III relies on.

lessons.title: Recommender Systems
lessons.lead: Feeds, stores, streaming, ads and search are recommendation problems. They are among the most valuable ML systems in industry and a favourite topic in system-design interviews.

lessons.title: Bayesian ML & Gaussian Processes
lessons.lead: Point estimates say what the model thinks; Bayesian methods also say how sure it is. Uncertainty matters for medicine, active learning, Bayesian optimization and safe decision-making.

lessons.title: Hyperparameter Optimization & AutoML
lessons.lead: Tuning by hand wastes time and compute. Learn which knobs matter and use search algorithms for the rest.

lessons.title: Causal Inference & Experimentation
lessons.lead: Predictive models learn correlations. Product and policy decisions need causes: "if we ship this feature, what happens?" Big tech runs thousands of experiments a year, and AI engineers are expected to read them correctly.

courses.title: Deep Learning
courses.tagline: Backpropagation to Transformers, built from scratch.
courses.description: How neural networks learn, why training works or fails, and the architectures behind modern AI: CNNs, RNNs, attention and the Transformer, graph networks, state space models and self-supervision.
outcomes: Derive backpropagation and build a network in NumPy
Train deep networks reliably: initialization, normalization, regularization
Implement CNNs, LSTMs and a GPT-style Transformer in PyTorch
Explain GNNs, state space models and self-supervised learning
Compress models with distillation, pruning and quantization

lessons.title: Neurons, MLPs & Activation Functions
lessons.lead: A neural network is a composition of simple functions: linear maps interleaved with nonlinearities.

lessons.title: Backpropagation, Derived and Built
lessons.lead: The algorithm that trains every neural network. It is the chain rule, organized so that the full gradient costs about the same as one forward pass.

lessons.title: Training Deep Networks: Init, Normalization, Regularization
lessons.lead: Backprop gives gradients; these techniques make sure the gradients are usable and the model generalizes.

lessons.title: The Complete PyTorch Training Loop
lessons.lead: This template, with small changes, trains almost every model you'll build.

lessons.title: Convolutional Neural Networks
lessons.lead: Images have local structure, and the same pattern can appear anywhere. Convolutions build both facts into the architecture.

lessons.title: Recurrent Networks, LSTMs & GRUs
lessons.lead: For sequences, carry a hidden state forward through time. Transformers have largely replaced RNNs, but RNNs explain why attention was needed, and state-space models are bringing recurrence back.

lessons.title: Attention & the Transformer
lessons.lead: The architecture behind GPT, BERT, ViT, Whisper, and almost every frontier model. Learn this lesson line by line.

toc.text: The Transformer block (pre-norm, as in GPT-style models)

lessons.title: Graph Neural Networks
lessons.lead: Molecules, social networks, road maps, citation graphs, fraud rings and knowledge graphs are not grids or sequences. GNNs learn from graph structure directly.

lessons.title: Efficient Sequence Models: Linear Attention & State Space Models
lessons.lead: Attention costs \(O(n^2)\) in sequence length. For very long contexts, audio, genomics and fast inference, researchers revived recurrence in a trainable, parallel form.

lessons.title: Self-Supervised & Representation Learning
lessons.lead: Labels are expensive; raw data is nearly free. Self-supervised learning invents a prediction task from the data itself and produces representations that transfer to many downstream tasks. Every foundation model is trained this way.

lessons.title: Model Compression: Pruning, Distillation & Quantization
lessons.lead: Production models must fit latency, memory and cost budgets, often on phones or a single GPU. Compression keeps most of the accuracy at a fraction of the cost.

courses.title: Computer Vision
courses.tagline: Classification, detection, segmentation, vision Transformers and 3D.
courses.description: Turning pixels into understanding: transfer learning, detectors and segmenters, ViT and CLIP, video, tracking, 3D reconstruction and document AI.
outcomes: Fine-tune pretrained backbones with sensible augmentation
Explain how detectors and segmenters work and evaluate them
Use ViT and CLIP, including zero-shot classification
Understand video models, tracking, NeRF and OCR pipelines

lessons.title: Images, Augmentation & Transfer Learning
lessons.lead: You will rarely train a vision model from scratch. You'll start from a pretrained backbone and adapt it.

lessons.title: Object Detection & Segmentation
lessons.lead: From "what is in the image" to "where exactly is it".

lessons.title: Vision Transformers, CLIP & Self-Supervised Vision
lessons.lead: Transformers took over vision too, and contrastive learning connected images to language.

lessons.title: Video, 3D, Tracking & Document Vision
lessons.lead: Beyond single images: motion, depth, geometry, and the messy real-world task of reading documents.

courses.title: NLP & Speech
courses.tagline: Text and speech, from TF-IDF to pretrained Transformers.
courses.description: How machines read and listen: classic text models, embeddings, tokenization, BERT-style encoders, speech recognition, information extraction, and the special challenges of Arabic and other languages.
outcomes: Build strong text baselines with TF-IDF and linear models
Explain word embeddings and subword tokenization
Fine-tune pretrained encoders for classification and NER
Process speech with spectrograms, CTC and encoder–decoder models
Handle Arabic script, dialects and multilingual evaluation

lessons.title: Classic NLP: Bag of Words, TF-IDF & n-gram Models
lessons.lead: Simple text representations are still strong baselines and power the keyword side of search (BM25, Lesson 8.2).

lessons.title: Word Embeddings: word2vec & GloVe
lessons.lead: "You shall know a word by the company it keeps." Learn dense vectors so that words appearing in similar contexts get similar vectors.

lessons.title: Subword Tokenization: BPE & Friends
lessons.lead: Models see tokens, not characters or words. Tokenization decides vocabulary size, sequence length, cost, and how well rare words and other languages are handled.

lessons.title: Pretrained Transformers: BERT, GPT & T5
lessons.lead: Pretrain once on huge unlabeled text, then adapt to any task with little labeled data. This is the transfer-learning revolution of NLP.

lessons.title: Speech & Audio
lessons.lead: Voice assistants, transcription, dubbing, call analytics and audio LLMs all start from a 1-D waveform and the same few transformations.

lessons.title: Information Extraction & Structured Prediction
lessons.lead: Turning unstructured text into structured records (entities, relations, fields) is one of the most common business uses of NLP: invoices, contracts, CVs, medical notes, support tickets.

lessons.title: Arabic & Multilingual NLP
lessons.lead: Most NLP research is in English, but most of the world is not. Arabic adds rich morphology, optional diacritics, many dialects and two scripts in daily use, and it is a great case study for building multilingual systems.

courses.title: Large Language Models
courses.tagline: How LLMs are trained, aligned, served and evaluated.
courses.description: The full life of a large language model: pretraining and scaling laws, decoding, fine-tuning with LoRA, alignment with RLHF and DPO, efficient inference, multimodality, reasoning, evaluation, and training your own small model.
outcomes: Explain pretraining, scaling laws and modern architectures
Control generation with temperature, top-k and top-p
Fine-tune with LoRA and QLoRA and reason about memory
Describe RLHF, DPO and RL for reasoning
Evaluate LLMs and train a small GPT end to end

lessons.title: How LLMs Are Built: Objective, Data & Scaling
lessons.lead: An LLM is a decoder-only Transformer trained to predict the next token on a very large amount of text. Capabilities come from scale, data quality, and post-training.

lessons.title: Decoding: Temperature, Top-k & Top-p
lessons.lead: The model outputs a distribution over the next token. How you pick from it changes everything about the output.

lessons.title: Fine-Tuning, LoRA & Quantization
lessons.lead: Adapting a large model on one GPU is possible because of two ideas: train a low-rank update instead of the whole matrix, and store weights in fewer bits.

lessons.title: Alignment: RLHF, DPO & RL for Reasoning
lessons.lead: Pretraining teaches a model what text looks like. Post-training teaches it which responses people actually want.

lessons.title: Inference Efficiency: KV Cache, FlashAttention & MoE
lessons.lead: Serving LLMs is a memory-bandwidth problem. These techniques are why chat models respond quickly and affordably.

lessons.title: Using LLMs Well: Prompting, Structured Output & Evaluation
lessons.lead: Most applied AI work today is building reliable systems around existing models.

lessons.title: Multimodal Models
lessons.lead: Modern assistants see images, read documents, hear speech and talk back. Most of them are built by connecting pretrained encoders to an LLM.

lessons.title: Reasoning & Test-Time Compute
lessons.lead: A model can trade more computation at inference time for better answers. This became a central scaling axis next to model size and data.

lessons.title: Evaluation, Safety & Interpretability
lessons.lead: How do we know a model is good, safe, and why it does what it does? These are open research problems and daily engineering work at AI labs.

lessons.title: Project: Train a Small LLM End to End
lessons.lead: Putting Parts IV and VII together: tokenizer, data pipeline, GPT model, training loop, evaluation and sampling. Run it on a single GPU in an afternoon.

courses.title: RAG, Agents & LLMOps
courses.tagline: Connect models to your data and tools, then ship them.
courses.description: The applied core of modern AI engineering: vector search, hybrid retrieval and reranking, RAG pipelines and their evaluation, agents and MCP, and running LLM applications in production.
outcomes: Build vector search with the right ANN index
Combine BM25, dense retrieval and rerankers
Build and evaluate a RAG pipeline with citations
Design reliable agents with tools and guardrails
Control latency and cost in production LLM apps

lessons.title: Embeddings & Vector Search
lessons.lead: Semantic search turns "find documents about X" into "find vectors close to X's vector".

lessons.title: Retrieval & Ranking: BM25, Hybrid Search, Rerankers
lessons.lead: Dense vectors capture meaning; keyword search catches exact names, codes and rare terms. The best systems combine them, then rerank.

toc.text: Hybrid search with Reciprocal Rank Fusion

lessons.title: Building a RAG Pipeline
lessons.lead: Retrieval-augmented generation: find relevant passages, put them in the prompt, and have the model answer from them with citations.

lessons.title: Evaluating Retrieval & RAG
lessons.lead: Measure retrieval and generation separately: a perfect generator can't fix a retriever that missed the right passage.

toc.text: Retrieval metrics (need labelled relevant passages per query)

lessons.title: Agents & Tool Use
lessons.lead: An agent is an LLM in a loop: decide on an action, call a tool, observe the result, repeat until done.

lessons.title: Agent Architectures, MCP & Reliability
lessons.lead: Moving from a demo agent to one people can depend on: choosing the right pattern, designing tools, connecting systems through standard protocols, and making failures safe.

toc.text: Tools and the Model Context Protocol

lessons.title: LLMOps: Shipping LLM Applications
lessons.lead: Latency, cost, quality and safety in production. This is the day-to-day job of many AI engineers.

courses.title: Generative Models
courses.tagline: VAEs, GANs, diffusion and flow matching.
courses.description: Models that learn the data distribution itself: autoencoders and the ELBO, adversarial training, diffusion and score-based models, normalizing flows, flow matching and token-based generation.
outcomes: Derive the ELBO and the reparameterization trick
Explain the GAN game and its failure modes
Implement the diffusion training objective and sampler
Compare flows, flow matching and autoregressive generation

lessons.title: Autoencoders & Variational Autoencoders
lessons.lead: Compress data to a latent code and reconstruct it. Make the latent space probabilistic and you get a generative model.

lessons.title: Generative Adversarial Networks
lessons.lead: Two networks in a game: a generator makes fakes, a discriminator tries to spot them. Both improve until fakes look real.

lessons.title: Diffusion Models
lessons.lead: Learn to reverse a gradual noising process. Start from pure noise, denoise step by step, and an image appears. This powers modern image, video and audio generation.

lessons.title: Normalizing Flows, Flow Matching & Token-Based Generation
lessons.lead: Three more ways to build a generative model: invertible transformations with exact likelihoods, learned velocity fields (behind many recent image and video models), and plain next-token prediction over learned discrete codes.

courses.title: Reinforcement Learning
courses.tagline: Learning from rewards: MDPs to PPO and AlphaZero.
courses.description: Agents that act and learn from the consequences: Bellman equations, Q-learning, policy gradients, actor–critic and PPO, deep RL, planning with tree search, and imitation learning.
outcomes: Write Bellman equations and run value iteration
Implement Q-learning and explain DQN
Derive the policy gradient and the PPO objective
Understand MCTS, imitation and offline RL

lessons.title: MDPs, Bellman Equations & Q-Learning
lessons.lead: An agent acts, the world responds with a new state and a reward, and the agent learns to maximize long-term reward.

lessons.title: Policy Gradients, Actor–Critic & PPO
lessons.lead: Instead of learning values and acting greedily, directly adjust the policy's parameters to make good actions more likely. This is the family used to fine-tune LLMs.

lessons.title: Deep RL, Planning & Imitation
lessons.lead: Combining RL with neural networks gave game-playing systems, robotic control and the post-training methods behind modern LLMs. This lesson covers the algorithms you'll meet in papers and libraries.

courses.title: Robotics & Embodied AI
courses.tagline: Kinematics, estimation, control, planning and robot learning.
courses.description: AI that moves in the physical world. The classical robotics stack (transforms, filters, controllers, planners) and how learning, simulation and foundation models are changing it.
outcomes: Compute forward and inverse kinematics with transforms
Derive and implement a Kalman filter
Tune PID controllers and explain LQR and MPC
Plan paths with A* and RRT
Explain imitation learning, sim-to-real and vision-language-action models

lessons.title: Rigid-Body Motion & Kinematics
lessons.lead: Before a robot can learn anything, it has to know where its parts are. Rotations, homogeneous transforms and kinematics are the coordinate geometry of embodied AI.

lessons.title: State Estimation: Kalman & Particle Filters
lessons.lead: Sensors are noisy and the world is only partly observed. Filters fuse predictions and measurements into the best estimate of where the robot really is.

lessons.title: Feedback Control: PID, LQR & MPC
lessons.lead: Knowing where you are and where you want to be is not enough: control turns the error between them into motor commands that are fast, stable and safe.

lessons.title: Motion Planning: A*, RRT & Trajectories
lessons.lead: Planning finds a collision-free path through space, then a smooth trajectory along it. Search and sampling algorithms are the classic tools.

lessons.title: Robot Learning: Imitation, Sim-to-Real & Foundation Models
lessons.lead: Learning lets robots pick up skills that are hard to program by hand. This lesson connects RL, imitation and large pretrained models to physical machines.

toc.text: Why learning for robots is hard
The modern recipe for a manipulation skill

courses.title: MLOps & Responsible AI
courses.tagline: Ship models, monitor them, and make sure they are fair and explainable.
courses.description: Everything after training: reproducibility, serving, containers, monitoring and drift, fairness metrics, explainability with SHAP, privacy, and data-centric practices like labelling and active learning.
outcomes: Package and serve a model behind an API with Docker
Detect data and concept drift
Measure fairness and explain predictions
Improve models by improving data

lessons.title: From Notebook to Production
lessons.lead: Reproducible training, a serving API, containers, and monitoring for when the world changes.

lessons.title: Fairness, Explainability & Privacy
lessons.lead: Models affect people. You need tools to check who they fail, why they decide what they decide, and what they leak.

toc.text: Fairness metrics (group AAA, prediction Y^\hat YY^)

lessons.title: Data-Centric AI: Labels, Quality & Synthetic Data
lessons.lead: Holding the model fixed and improving the data is often the fastest path to better results. Strong AI engineers are deliberate about how data is collected, labelled and cleaned.

courses.title: AI Security & Safety
courses.tagline: Attacks on AI systems and the defences that hold up.
courses.description: How models and AI applications get attacked and how to defend them: adversarial examples, data poisoning and backdoors, privacy attacks, prompt injection against agents, and governance practices for shipping responsibly.
outcomes: Generate adversarial examples and explain adversarial training
Recognize poisoning, backdoors and membership inference
Defend LLM apps and agents against prompt injection
Write model cards and run a basic AI risk assessment

lessons.title: Adversarial Examples & Robustness
lessons.lead: A perturbation too small to see can flip a confident prediction. Understanding why is the starting point of AI security.

toc.text: Why they exist: the linear view

lessons.title: Poisoning, Backdoors & Privacy Attacks
lessons.lead: Attacks on the training pipeline and on what a model remembers: corrupted data, hidden triggers, membership inference, extraction, and the defences that work.

lessons.title: LLM Security: Prompt Injection, Jailbreaks & Agents
lessons.lead: When a model reads untrusted text and can take actions, every web page and document becomes a possible attacker. This is the most practical security topic for AI engineers today.

toc.text: Why LLM apps need their own security model

lessons.title: AI Governance, Risk & Documentation
lessons.lead: Shipping AI responsibly means knowing what can go wrong, writing it down, and meeting the rules that apply. This lesson covers the practices teams actually use.

courses.title: Systems & Scale
courses.tagline: GPUs, distributed training and ML system design.
courses.description: What top AI teams expect beyond modelling: how GPUs execute work, how to train across many GPUs, and how to design complete ML systems under real constraints.
outcomes: Reason about compute-bound vs memory-bound workloads
Choose between data, tensor, pipeline and sharded parallelism
Run a structured ML system design interview
Do back-of-the-envelope capacity estimates

lessons.title: GPUs, Memory & Kernels
lessons.lead: Deep learning is matrix multiplication at scale. Knowing where time goes on a GPU explains FlashAttention, quantization, batching, and why some "fast" models are slow.

lessons.title: Distributed Training
lessons.lead: Frontier models are trained on thousands of GPUs. Even fine-tuning a 7B model needs more than one. You should understand every parallelism strategy and its cost.

lessons.title: ML System Design
lessons.lead: Senior interviews and real projects both ask: design a system that solves this business problem with ML. The structure of your answer matters as much as the model.

toc.text: A framework for any design question

lessons.title: System Design Case Studies
lessons.lead: Five classic designs, condensed. Practise each one out loud in 35–45 minutes using the framework from 12.3.

courses.title: Career & Interviews
courses.tagline: The roadmap, the interviews, the portfolio, and how to keep learning.
courses.description: How to turn everything you learn here into a job: a week-by-week roadmap, how AI engineering interviews work, what makes a portfolio stand out, and how to read papers efficiently.
outcomes: Plan your study path and checkpoints
Prepare for coding, ML, system design and behavioural rounds
Build portfolio projects that hiring managers notice
Read and reproduce research papers efficiently

lessons.title: The Roadmap: From Zero to Job-Ready
lessons.lead: A week-by-week path through every course in this academy, with a project at the end of each phase. Already strong in an area? Skim its lessons, pass the quizzes and move on.

lessons.title: How Top Companies Interview AI Engineers
lessons.lead: Loops differ by company and role (research engineer, ML engineer, applied AI engineer), but the building blocks are consistent.

lessons.title: Portfolio, Projects & Getting Hired
lessons.lead: Hiring managers look for evidence that you can take a messy problem to a working, measured system. Three excellent projects beat thirty tutorials.

toc.text: What makes a project stand out

lessons.title: Reading Papers & Staying Current
lessons.lead: The field moves monthly. The skill that compounds is reading papers efficiently and reproducing what matters.
